name: Choosing Subtree is Fun
description: There is a tree consisting of n vertices. The vertices are numbered from 1 to n . Let's define the length of an interval [ l , r ] as the value r - l + 1 . The score of a subtree of this tree is the maximum length of such an interval [ l , r ] that, the vertices with numbers l , l + 1, ..., r belong to the subtree. Considering all subtrees of the tree whose size is at most k , return the maximum score of the subtree. Note, that in this problem tree is not rooted, so a subtree — is an arbitrary connected subgraph of the tree.
input_specification: There are two integers in the first line, n and k ( 1 ≤ k ≤ n ≤ 10 5 ). Each of the next n - 1 lines contains integers a i and b i ( 1 ≤ a i , b i ≤ n , a i ≠ b i ). That means a i and b i are connected by a tree edge. It is guaranteed that the input represents a tree.
output_specification: Output should contain a single integer — the maximum possible score.
approach_summary: Exploit monotonicity of two-pointer invariant [L, R]. Advance R while shifting L forward to maintain validity, running in O(N) amortized time.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 372D — Choosing Subtree is Fun [34. Two Pointers]
topic_editorial.key_invariant: When scanning contiguous subarrays or paired indices, advancing the right pointer $R$ monotonically tightens or relaxes the constraint, allowing the left pointer $L$ to only advance forward without ever needing to reset backwards.
